notes: Havant operates mandatory HMO licensing only. No selective or additional licensing scheme was found. The published HMO fee schedule contains only mandatory occupancy bands, and the council's licensing A-Z has no property licensing entry at all.
research: The only property-licensing page frames the scheme purely as the national statutory duty: 'It is a statutory requirement for us to operate a licensing scheme for HMOs with five or more people, from two or more households - as of October 2018'. FEE CORROBORATION: the same page carries the complete published fee list and every line is a mandatory occupancy band with no discretionary line: 5 occupants £817.09; 6-10 £873.66; 11-15 £984.64; 16-20 £1,302.34; 20+ at an additional hourly rate, for a 5-year licence. SITE SEARCH: a search for 'selective licensing' returned 'Your search yielded no results.' A search for 'additional licensing' returned five results, none about property licensing (hackney carriage drivers, the mandatory HMO page, club premises certificates, knowledge test, keeping primates). SUPPORTING: the private sector housing hub links to six sub-pages, none a discretionary scheme; the licensing A-Z lists only alcohol, gaming, hackney carriage and 'other licences and permits' with no property licensing category. TRAP: the phrase 'we operate a licensing scheme' reads like a discretionary designation but is explicitly the national mandatory duty from October 2018. CAVEAT: Havant publishes no explicit denial; the finding rests on convergent absence across the HMO page, fee schedule, housing hub, licensing A-Z and two site searches.

notes: Herefordshire operates mandatory HMO licensing only. No selective or additional licensing scheme was found. The single published licence fee of about £1,404 for five years covers mandatory HMO licensing alone.
research: The licensing directory entry describes the mandatory threshold only: 'any property that is let to five people or more, in two separate households, who share either bathroom or cooking facilities, will now require to be licenced', effective 1 October 2018, removing the previous three-storey test. FEE CORROBORATION: a basic application fee for a 5-year licence of £1,404 from 1 April 2026, with a 5% discount for accredited landlords and 15% for renewals, stackable to 25%. One fee stream only; no discretionary licensing fee line. SITE SEARCH: 'selective licensing' returned 3 results, none relevant. TRAP, IMPORTANT: a search for 'additional licensing private rented' surfaced a committee decision 'REVISION AND CONSOLIDATION OF HEREFORDSHIRE AMENITY STANDARDS' citing the 'Multiple Occupation (Additional Provisions) (England) Regulations 2007'. That is the HMO amenity and space standards regulation, NOT Part 2 s.56 additional licensing. Any keyword matcher combining 'additional' plus 'licensing' plus 'HMO' would false-positive here. SUPPORTING: the housing hub's Landlords section contains only three items (HMO licensing, the landlord account, the deposit/bond scheme) and the landlord advice page covers HHSRS and enforcement with no licensing scheme. CAVEAT: no explicit council disclaimer exists.

notes: Hertsmere operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for 5 or more people in 2 or more households, fee £1,306. No selective or additional scheme. A 2026 Article 4 Direction covering Potters Bar wards is planning control over HMO conversion, not licensing.
research: The HMO licensing page sets the requirement as 'Which properties need licensing? ... Properties occupied by five or more people in two or more households', the plain mandatory threshold with no lowered trigger. FEE CORROBORATION: 'New and renewal applications Up to five people £1,306.00'; 'Every additional person over five £105.00'; variation £366.00. Only mandatory fee lines exist. MAJOR TRAP IDENTIFIED AND EXCLUDED: 'The Hertsmere Borough Council (Houses in Multiple Occupation) (Potters Bar) Article 4 Direction 2026'. This is a PLANNING Article 4 Direction, not licensing. The council's own wording: 'An Article 4 Direction is a legal mechanism used by local authorities that removes permitted development rights.' It addresses planning Use Class conversions from C3 to C4. It is a non-immediate direction made 23 April 2026, consulted 6 May to 17 June 2026, and 'will come into force on 06 May 2027, if confirmed'. It names four wards: Potters Bar Parkfield, Potters Bar Oakmere, Potters Bar Furzefield, Bentley Heath and The Royds. Because it names wards AND carries three dates AND is dated in the future, it is the single most dangerous false positive in this batch and could easily be miscoded as an 'upcoming' licensing scheme. SECOND TRAP: a news item on 'proposed amenity standards for houses in multiple occupation' concerns amenity and space standards, not a designation. SITE SEARCH: the working parameter is '?term='; a search for 'selective licensing' returns one result, 'Apply for a Film Classification'. The full sitemap contains zero occurrences of 'selective'. SUPPORTING: the private sector housing hub lists eight pages under Housing Enforcement, none a discretionary scheme.

notes: High Peak operates mandatory HMO licensing only, £450 for a first five-year licence. No selective or additional scheme was found. The council's private rented homes page sets out landlord duties with no licensing or registration requirement.
research: The HMO page describes the mandatory scheme only: 'any property that is let to 5 or more unrelated persons who are living as two or more separate households and who share either bathroom or cooking facilities will now require to be licenced by the Local Authority'. FEE CORROBORATION: first application £450.00 for five years; renewal £350.00; change of licence holder £350.00. No discretionary fee line. Non-compliance carries 'a civil penalty up to £30,000 or, if prosecuted, an unlimited fine'. Licensing is run by the Private Sector Housing Service with no geographic limitation. STRONGEST NEGATIVE: the dedicated Private rented homes page sets out landlord obligations at length, covering the Renters' Rights Act 2025, deposit protection, energy efficiency standards and letting agent redress, and contains no licensing or registration requirement of any kind. A live selective scheme would necessarily be flagged there. SUPPORTING: the landlord hub links only to HMO, empty properties, private rented homes, empty-home reuse, enforcement, grant assistance and registered providers; the enforcement page covers empty-property powers with no licensing scheme. CAVEAT STATED PLAINLY: the site search endpoint could not be located, with several patterns returning 404, so no keyword sweep was possible. This is evidentially the weakest negative in this batch, though the topic pages and fee schedule are consistent.

notes: Hinckley and Bosworth operates mandatory HMO licensing only. The council states you do not need a licence to rent out all HMOs in the borough. No selective or additional scheme. Fees are roughly £800 for a small HMO and £1,000 for a large one.
research: This council gives the clearest wording in the batch and the closest thing to an explicit disclaimer: 'you don't need a licence to rent out all HMOs in the borough of Hinckley and Bosworth'. The same page sets the mandatory test with both conditions required: 'There are five or more occupants living in the property' AND 'Two or more separate households live in the property'. That wording specifically rules out an additional licensing designation, which by definition would extend licensing to smaller HMOs of 3 or 4 occupants, and it applies borough-wide. FEE CORROBORATION: 'Typically, the cost for a new five-year licence on a small HMO is around £800 and a large HMO £1000', calculated per property by size, layout, escape routes and risk, with a £75 discount for online application. No discretionary licensing fee appears. SUPPORTING: the private housing hub links to landlord advice, tenant advice, HMO licensing, empty homes, grants, UK entry clearance inspections and the enforcement policy. The landlord advice page mentions no licensing or registration requirement at all. STRUCTURAL CHECK: the HMO section is a five-tab structure with no sixth tab or sibling page for any other licensing type.

notes: Huntingdonshire operates mandatory HMO licensing only, £705 initial and £375 renewal. No selective or additional scheme appears in the council's full licence A-Z, its fee schedule or its housing policy library.
research: EXHAUSTIVE LICENCE A-Z: the council lists every licence it issues (Club Premises Certificate, Personal Licences, Premises Licences, Regulated Entertainment, TENs, Animal Boarding, Dog Breeding, Pet Shops, Riding Establishments, Caravan and Camping Sites, Charity Market Stalls, Cooling Towers, Dangerous Wild Animals, Food Business Registration, Food Premises Approval, Gambling, House to House Collections, Houses in Multiple Occupation, Lotteries, Pavement Licences, Scrap Metal Dealers, Sex Establishments, Stage Hypnotism, Street Collections, Street Trading, Tattooing and Piercing, Taxis and Private Hire, Zoos). No selective, additional or private rented property licensing appears anywhere in that complete list. MANDATORY THRESHOLD ONLY: 'property occupied by five or more people forming two or more separate households, regardless of the number of storeys, or' / 'purpose-built flat in a block of up to two flats and occupied as an HMO by five or more people' - verbatim the national mandatory scope under the 2018 Prescribed Description Order. FEE CORROBORATION: initial £705; renewal £375; revocation £185; variation (simple) £75; variation (large) £225; £165 per officer visit. No discretionary licensing fee. SUPPORTING: the landlord advice page covers Housing Standards, Landlord Accreditation, Eviction, Deposit Schemes and Right to Rent, and on licensing says only 'Go to the HMO page to find out more.' The housing policy library lists seven documents with no licensing designation or policy. CAVEAT: no explicit denial is published; the finding is convergent absence across the licence A-Z, the mandatory-only scope, the fee schedule and the policy library.

notes: Ipswich operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for 5 or more people from different households since October 2018, at £155 per unit. No selective or additional scheme. The Article 4 area requiring planning permission for 3+ person HMOs is planning control, not licensing.
research: Checked with particular care and verified twice independently, both passes agreeing. THRESHOLD IS UNAMBIGUOUSLY MANDATORY, WITH A DATE: 'From 1st October 2018, it is mandatory for landlords of Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) occupied by five or more people from different households to obtain an HMO licence'. FEE CORROBORATION: 'The full licence fee for a House in Multiple Occupation is £155 per unit of accommodation', payable in two parts since 1 October 2020. No discretionary licensing fee line. Note the page also carries a stale worked example that does not reconcile at £155/unit; treat £155/unit as the headline. SITE SEARCH AND SITEMAP: a search for 'selective licensing' returns 'Your search yielded no results.' The full sitemap contains ZERO occurrences of 'selective'. LICENCE A-Z: lists sex establishments, skips, building control, skin piercing, industrial licences, mobile/park home licence, HMO licence (described as 'mandatory HMO licensing requirements') and pleasure boat licences. DECISION REGISTER: the delegated decisions register covering 7 August 2020 to 6 August 2026 contains no selective or additional licensing designation and no consultation authorisation. A Part 3 designation is a formal executive decision and would necessarily appear. CONSULTATIONS: no selective-licensing consultation, current or closed; the only licensing item is a closed alcohol Cumulative Impact Assessment. TRAP 1, ALMOST CERTAINLY THE SOURCE OF ANY 'IPSWICH HAS SELECTIVE LICENSING' CLAIM: an Article 4 Direction in force 1 June 2024 covering 12 wards (Alexandra, Bixley, Bridge, Castle Hill, Gainsborough, Gipping, Holywells, Priory Heath, Rushmere, St John's, St Margaret's, Westgate), which 'removes existing permitted development rights for material changes of use from dwelling houses (C3 use class) to small houses of multiple occupation (C4 use class)'. In that area planning permission is required for HMOs with three or more unrelated individuals. Planning control, NOT licensing, and routinely misreported as 'Ipswich licenses 3+ HMOs'. TRAP 2: the HMO landing page carries loose wording implying three or more people requires a licence; that is the s.254 definition with the licensing caveat elided. LIMIT: the ModernGov keyword endpoint is POST/JS-driven and the decisions register begins August 2020, so a pre-2020 abandoned consultation cannot be fully excluded.

notes: Isle of Wight operates mandatory HMO licensing only. The council's own site search returns no results at all for selective licensing or property licensing. No scheme found. The council does not publish HMO fees online and directs enquiries to 01983 823040.
research: ACCESS NOTE, IMPORTANT FOR REPEAT RUNS: iow.gov.uk returns HTTP 403 to automated fetchers because its robots.txt explicitly disallows AI crawlers including ClaudeBot and GPTBot. Plain curl with a standard browser user-agent returns HTTP 200 normally. This council is therefore VERIFIED, not unverified; the 403 is a bot block and carries no information about licensing. Every finding was re-run and independently confirmed by direct curl. THE COUNCIL'S OWN SEARCH INDEX IS THE PRIMARY EVIDENCE, and it indexes PDFs as well as pages (it surfaces corporate plans and consultation PDFs), so a nil return is meaningful: a search for 'selective licensing' returns verbatim 'Searching on "selective licensing" found no results'. A search for 'property licensing' returns 'found no results'. TRAP: a search for 'additional licensing' returns one result, and that single hit is a planning consultation PDF about great crested newt DISTRICT LICENSING, an ecology matter with no connection to housing. A search for 'licensing scheme' returns 6 results, all the same newt district licensing scheme plus Corporate Plan PDFs. Any keyword matcher on 'additional licensing' would false-positive on the newt documents here. HMO PAGE: 'A house in multiple occupancy is one property with three or more tenants, who are a part of more than one household (not family), that share a toilet, bathroom, or kitchen. A large HMO has five or more tenants.' The 'three or more' figure is the s.254 statutory DEFINITION, not a licensing threshold. EVIDENTIAL WEAKNESS STATED PLAINLY: the fee-schedule test CANNOT be applied here, because the council publishes no HMO fee schedule at all, directing enquiries to a phone number, and its general licensing fees page contains zero occurrences of HMO, houses in multiple, housing or selective. The negative rests on the zero-result search index plus the mandatory-only HMO page. RESIDUAL RISK: ModernGov committee papers were not exhaustively read.

council: Council of the Isles of Scilly
notes: The Isles of Scilly operates mandatory HMO licensing only. Its public HMO register cites the Housing Act 2004 and lists licensed HMOs only. No selective or additional licensing scheme was found.
research: MANDATORY THRESHOLD ONLY: a licence is required where 'it's rented to 5 or more people who form more than 1 household' together with sharing or lack of amenities, and the building height requirement was removed on 1 October 2018. Enforcement wording: 'The Council can issue a Civil Penalty Notice upto £30,000 for offences relating to licensing and management of HMO's.' REGISTER CORROBORATION: the public register states 'This register is required under the Housing Act 2004 Part ll and shows all HMO's in the Council of the Isles of Scilly area that are currently licenced.' The register is scoped to Part 2 mandatory licensing; there is no Part 3 selective register, which s.232 would require if a selective scheme existed. SITEMAP SWEEP: the full sitemap contains ZERO occurrences of 'selective'. The private sector housing branch contains fourteen pages, none a licensing designation, and the licensing branch contains only alcohol, gambling, street trading, sex establishment and boatman licences. TRAP: the housing landing page references a 'Responsible Landlord Scheme'. This is a voluntary accreditation initiative, not a Housing Act 2004 designation. CONTEXT: the Isles of Scilly is England's smallest authority, roughly 2,200 residents, and a selective licensing designation here would be highly implausible; the site evidence is consistent with mandatory-only.

council: Borough Council of King's Lynn and West Norfolk
notes: King's Lynn and West Norfolk operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for 5 or more occupants, with fees of £768 to £1,415 by bedroom count. No selective or additional scheme. The 3 or more people figure on the council site is the HMO definition, not a licensing threshold.
research: MANDATORY THRESHOLD, STATED EXPLICITLY: 'All Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) occupied by five or more people require an HMO licence', plus any single flat that is an HMO unless in a purpose-built block of three or more flats, with exemptions for housing associations, councils, health authorities, police and fire services. KEY TRAP AVOIDED, AND THE COUNCIL ITSELF DISAMBIGUATES IT: another page says 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) are properties rented out to three or more people who do not form the same household [and] share facilities such as a bathroom or kitchen', immediately followed by 'the criteria we use when deciding whether to licence an HMO is different to the HMO definition above.' The 'three or more' figure is the s.254 DEFINITION, not a licensing threshold. This is a high-risk false positive for any automated scraper. FEE CORROBORATION: new licence 3 to 15 bedrooms, £768 to £1,415 banded by bedroom count; renewal £649 to £1,135; 'There is currently no fee for the variation of an HMO licence.' No discretionary licensing fee line. REGISTER SCOPE: 'The public register for mandatory licensed HMOs is not available online.' The register is labelled mandatory-only; s.232 would require a register for a discretionary scheme too, and none is published. LICENCE A-Z: lists thirteen licence types with no property licensing entry at all. SITEMAP SWEEP: the landlord and housing branches contain no selective or additional licensing URL.

notes: Hull operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for 5 or more people in 2 or more households, at £225 plus a size-based fee. No selective or additional scheme is live. The Hull Accredited Landlord Scheme is voluntary, and the HMO Article 4 Direction is planning control.
research: HIGH PRIORITY council, verified twice independently, both passes agreeing. MANDATORY THRESHOLD ONLY: 'A property is classed as an HMO subject to licensing if it is occupied by 5 or more persons. These persons form 2 or more households, and they share a bathroom or kitchen.' FEE CORROBORATION, strongest evidence: fees are listed by bedroom count only, from 3 bed at '£225 + £629.50' up to 10 bed at '£225 + £823.75', plus '£27.75 per additional bedroom'. There is no selective or additional licensing fee line anywhere. Note the bands starting at 3 bedrooms reflect property size, not occupancy, and are consistent with mandatory-only since a 3-bedroom property can house 5 people. SITEMAP SWEEP: the full sitemap contains no URL matching selective or additional licensing, and direct probes of two plausible selective-licensing paths returned 404. LANDLORD AND TENANT HUBS BOTH SILENT: neither lists any licensing scheme, and the tenant hub lists 20 topics with no mention of licensed areas. A live scheme would have to be signposted to tenants as well as landlords. REGISTER: cites only s.232 and lists no designated wards, areas or streets. TRAP 1: the Hull Accredited Landlord Scheme appears prominently and reads like a scheme, but 'You can apply to join', i.e. voluntary accreditation, not a designation. TRAP 2: the HMO application page refers to 'an additional licensing fee invoice', meaning an extra fee, NOT Part 2 s.56. TRAP 3: Hull operates 27 Article 4 Directions and one is explicitly 'Houses in Multiple Occupation'. Planning control removing permitted development rights, in the council's own words: 'in some areas, mainly conservation areas, we have removed some of these rights by making Article 4 Directions.' HISTORICAL GAP STATED PLAINLY: Hull was flagged as historically operating selective licensing. No past designation could be confirmed or dated; there is no expired-scheme page, archive note or designation notice reachable on the domain, the site search returned 404 on every pattern tried, and the committee system failed with a TLS certificate error. The confident finding is that NO scheme is live now; historical dates are unverifiable and are not asserted.

council: Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames
notes: Kingston upon Thames operates mandatory HMO licensing only. The council says you will only need a licence if the property has 5 or more people forming 2 or more households. Fees are £319.40 new and £250 renewal per letting. No selective or additional scheme.
research: HIGH PRIORITY council, verified twice independently, both passes agreeing. Kingston is an exception to the usual London-borough pattern of running additional licensing. DECISIVE QUOTE: 'You'll only need a licence if your property has 5 or more people forming 2 or more households and sharing facilities'. The word 'only' plus the 5-person threshold rules out an additional licensing designation, which by definition captures smaller HMOs. The page also confirms 'Purpose-built blocks with 3+ flats don't require licensing'. FEE CORROBORATION: '£319.40 per letting for a new licence' and '£250 per letting to renew', with a £100 discount for accreditation members on new applications, 50 per cent for registered charities, and a £300 late-renewal penalty. Exactly one fee stream. SITEMAP SWEEP, decisive structural evidence: both pages of the sitemap were retrieved in full and the entire site contains ONE property licensing page, the mandatory HMO page. No URL containing 'selective' or 'additional' exists anywhere. The licensing A-Z lists 14 licence types with no discretionary property licensing. DOCUMENT LIBRARY: lists only HMO application, HMO Standards, self declaration, revocation, TEN and variation forms. No designation notice. MAJOR TRAP FLAGGED: the HMO enforcement options page contains the phrase 'offences in relation to licensing of houses under Part 3 of the Act (selective licensing)'. This is NOT evidence of a Kingston scheme. It is verbatim boilerplate from the statutory civil penalties guidance listing offence types, which every council reproduces whether or not it has designated anything. This is the single most likely source of an automated false positive for this borough. METHOD CAVEAT: Kingston's site search is broken for this purpose, returning an identical 3,261-result set for every query, so it was discarded entirely and the finding rests on full sitemap enumeration, the licensing A-Z, the fee schedule and the document library. The consultation portal did not resolve, so a scheme currently out to consultation cannot be fully excluded, though nothing on the main site hints at one.
